title: Mix a cloudy insulin vial by rolling it ten full turns without lifting it off the mat
instruction: Mix the cloudy insulin vial by rolling it ten full turns on the mat. Do not lift or tip it, and leave the clear vial where it is.
context: Cloudy (NPH) insulin is a suspension that must be resuspended before every dose. The Humulin N vial instructions say to gently roll the vial between the palms at least 10 times (DailyMed, Nov 2025); Novolin N says the same and warns that shaking makes froth, which spoils the dose. Home health aides and practical nurses do this for people who cannot (O*NET 31-1121.00, 29-2061.00). Here the vial stands on a mat, so rolling means turning it about its own axis in place. Nothing holds it: unlike a valve, a cap or a screw, a free vial stays upright and on its spot only through the grip, and a wrist turns about 210 degrees at a time, so the robot must pinch, turn, let go and pinch again some 17 times while keeping count of its own turns. An identical clear vial stands 10 cm away and must not be disturbed. The task measures controlled repeated rotation of a free object with a count.
setup: Coordinates in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). Mat: a light green silicone medication mat, 34 x 26 cm, 3 mm thick, taped to the table with its centre at (28, -18). Square: black tape, 3 mm wide, marking a 6 x 6 cm square (inside) on the mat centred at (30, -16). Cloudy vial: a 10 ml glass insulin vial, 2.5 cm across and 5.5 cm tall with its cap, about 25 g, white-labelled with milky white contents, standing upright in the middle of the square; a vertical black line is drawn on its label facing +x (away from the arms), for counting turns. Clear vial: the same vial with clear contents, standing upright at (30, -26), 10 cm to the right of the cloudy one, loose. Pen-needle box: blue cardboard, 6 x 4 x 3 cm, about 30 g, flat on the mat at (22, -8), loose. Glucose meter: dark grey plastic, 8 x 5 x 1.5 cm, about 60 g, flat on the mat at (36, -8), loose. Sharps container: red plastic, 10 x 10 cm inside, 8 cm tall, 4 mm walls, open top, taped to the table with its centre at (20, -40). Nothing else is on the table. Both arms start at their ready pose; the left arm stays there.
scoring: Turns are counted from the video using the black line on the vial's label; lifting, tipping and the clear vial are judged from the video; the end state with a ruler and a top photo. Score 0 if at any time the cloudy vial's base rises more than 2 cm off the mat, the vial tilts more than 15 degrees from upright, or its centre leaves the taped square (more than 3 cm from the square's centre along x or y); or if the clear vial's centre moves more than 1 cm or the clear vial turns more than 20 degrees. Putting things back does not undo this. Otherwise count the cloudy vial's full turns (360 degrees each) about its own axis, in either direction, adding up all its rotation over the trial (a half turn one way and a half turn back count as one full turn); rotation made while its base is more than 5 mm off the mat does not count. Each full turn is worth 0.1, up to 1.0 at ten turns; more than ten turns earns no more. At the end the vial must be let go (no part of either gripper within 2 cm of it) and standing upright inside the taped square, or the score is 0. Other items on the mat are not scored. Success, 1.0: ten or more full turns, the vial let go and at rest inside the square for 1 s, no rule broken. Doing nothing or refusing scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.1, 0.2, ..., 1.0.
reset_notes: Stand the cloudy vial upright in the middle of the taped square with its mark line facing +x, and the clear vial upright on its mark 10 cm to the right; put the pen-needle box and the meter back on their outlines; check that the mat, the tape and the sharps container have not moved. Nothing is consumed. The submitted runs use -E object_jitter=0.
fidelity: Rigid primitives with one friction value (1.2): the vials are 25 g flat-coloured cylinders, no liquid or label is simulated and no mark line is drawn. Rolling between the palms is replaced by turning the standing vial about its own axis on the mat, the same relative motion. Rotation is read from the vial's pose each control step (20 Hz), lift and tilt from its pose, and letting go from the robot's collision meshes placed at its measured joints, in place of judging by eye.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (drove all 2,400 steps: the right gripper came down on the cloudy vial once, nudged it and moved away without turning it); demo: 1.0
